_comment: The diagnostics corpus: a piece of .ctree source plus the set of diagnostics it must produce.
The set must match exactly, so one extra diagnostic is still a failure. The spec lists the checks, and anything beyond
that list is non-conformance rather than extra strictness.
The authoritative table of short codes is conformance/codes.json, and the full list of kinds is in docs/*/contract.md.
related is optional: a diagnostic may point at another place it is connected to, which DeadRule does when it points at the rule that covers it.
vocabulary is optional: when it is given the case runs check_with_vocabulary, and otherwise it runs plain check.

cases.name: lex/tab-indent
cases.note: §4.3 forbids tabs. Indentation stops counting at the tab, so this line lands in the scope of the anonymous root

cases.name: lex/line-without-a-symbol
cases.note: §4.1: a missing `-` must be an error and never a silent skip. The next line is indented with nothing claiming it, so it is reported as a jump too

cases.name: lex/symbol-without-space
cases.note: §4.1: a symbol must be followed by at least one space

cases.name: indent/base-must-be-a-power-of-two
cases.note: §4.3: the base may only be 2, 4 or 8

cases.name: indent/not-a-multiple-of-the-base
cases.note: The base is 2 and one line is indented 3, which is both a mix and one level too deep

cases.name: indent/child-jumps-a-level
cases.note: §4.3: the base is 2 and a grandchild indents straight to 6, crossing two levels

cases.name: structure/stop-path-may-not-have-children
cases.note: §4.2: `|` does not propagate, so declaring children under it contradicts what it means

cases.name: structure/rule-inside-a-target-block
cases.note: §4.2: only node declarations are allowed inside the block of a `>`, and that rule has no targets either

cases.name: structure/empty-document-is-a-warning
cases.note: An empty document is a warning, since there is simply nothing to do

cases.name: semantics/dead-rule-points-at-its-killer
cases.note: Two `@` rules of the same color in one scope, where the later one covers the earlier one completely

cases.name: semantics/conflicting-rules
cases.note: Two colors collide in one scope, where the author clearly mistyped one of them, so it is reported as a conflict rather than a dead rule

cases.name: semantics/redundant-rule
cases.note: An ancestor already passes red down, so writing another `@ red` is redundant

cases.name: semantics/fully-covered-rules-are-dead
cases.note: The later `@ delete` covers both earlier rules at once

cases.name: semantics/partially-covered-is-not-dead
cases.note: A rule is only dead under complete coverage, and here protect cuts through only part of it

cases.name: semantics/isolated-target-is-redundant
cases.note: `~` accepts no tint from an ancestor, and `>` travels exactly that channel, so the target is ignored.

cases.name: errors/all-of-them-in-one-pass
cases.note: All of them are reported in one pass instead of stopping at the first

cases.name: lex/names-are-opaque
cases.note: All five symbols, `#`, `/` and spaces may appear in a name, because a name runs to end of line and is not escaped
cases.source:
# a comment on a line of its own
- a>b
    @ red

    // a comment line may appear anywhere
    - a#b
        @ blue
    - with space/and slash
        @ blue

cases.name: lex/crlf-line-endings
cases.note: A checkout on Windows is all CRLF. The \r is part of the newline, so the name is `a`

cases.name: lex/no-trailing-newline
cases.note: The last line has no newline at the end, and it is still a complete line

cases.name: lex/utf8-bom
cases.note: Notepad writes a BOM by default. Without stripping it the first line counts as not starting with a symbol, and the whole document is wrong from line one

cases.name: lex/names-may-be-non-ascii
cases.note: A name is an opaque string, so non-ASCII is just as legal, and the same goes for a color

cases.name: lex/tab-on-a-blank-line-is-fine
cases.note: The indentation of blank and comment lines takes no part in the structure, so a leading tab has nothing to do with an unambiguous indent and must not be reported

cases.name: lex/tab-on-a-declaration-still-errors
cases.note: The other way round: a tab on a declaration line is still reported, so the case above must not be taken too far

cases.name: structure/duplicate-path-is-a-warning
cases.note: Declaring the same path twice is a warning: the rules in both declarations take part in evaluation and the later one settles the path type. It is a reminder that the author wrote it twice

cases.name: duplicate/both-declarations-execute
cases.note: `~` with `@` first and `>` second on the same path. Both rules reach that path, as the explanation chain shows, and the larger line number wins, so the `@ keep` under `~` is covered by the later `>`

cases.name: duplicate/last-declaration-sets-the-path-type
cases.note: The same two declarations in the opposite order: the last `~` settles the path type, so the target of the earlier `>` resolves to an isolated path and is ignored, which is last-definition-wins showing up in the structure

cases.name: duplicate/direct-child-and-a-target-block
cases.note: The same name written once inside the block of a `>` and once directly at the same level: they are two declarations of one path rather than two nodes
